housing.summary: Average 1-bedroom apartment in Regina city centre costs approximately CAD 1,481/month per Numbeo (Jun 2026). Saskatchewan landlords typically require first month's rent as deposit. Kijiji.ca is the main local rental portal.

banking.summary: Major Canadian banks serve Regina. To open an account as a newcomer, typical documents include passport, immigration document (work/study permit or PR card), proof of address, and SIN if available. RBC and Scotiabank both offer newcomer banking packages.
required_docs: Immigration document (work permit, study permit, or PR card)

schools.summary: Regina is served by Regina Public Schools and Regina Catholic School Division for K-12. International Baccalaureate (IB) programs are available at some secondary schools. The provincial curriculum is Saskatchewan-based.
curricula: International Baccalaureate (IB) at select secondary schools

legal_admin.summary: Newcomers on work or study permits must notify IRCC of address changes via the IRCC portal (ircc.canada.ca). Permanent residents register their SIN and may update address with Service Canada. Saskatchewan drivers must exchange a foreign licence within 90 days of establishing residency.
legal_admin.registration_step: Update address with IRCC at ircc.canada.ca if on work/study permit; permanent residents update SIN address at Service Canada.

tax_finance.summary: A Social Insurance Number (SIN) is Canada's tax identification number, issued by Service Canada. Required for work, tax filing, and government benefits. Apply at a Service Canada office or online.

transport.summary: Regina Transit operates the city's bus network. Adult monthly pass is CAD 97. Numbeo reports average pass at CAD 88-97. Newcomers must exchange foreign driving licences within 90 days via SGI Saskatchewan. Saskatchewan health card (SK Health Card) has a 3-month wait period for new arrivals from outside Canada.
transport.driving_licence_exchange: Foreign licence holders must exchange to a Saskatchewan licence within 90 days of establishing residency. Apply at an SGI (Saskatchewan Government Insurance) driver licensing office (sgi.sk.ca).
transport.healthcare_registration: Apply for a Saskatchewan Health Card via eHealth Saskatchewan (ehealthsask.ca). Coverage begins on or before the first day of the third month after arriving in Canada. Private insurance recommended during wait period.
